Hi Samir / Olivia —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery + proposed plan for the 3-week POC so we can align on success criteria and ownership. Please review and confirm or call out changes.

Recap (what we heard)
- Goal: Replace current customer-support summarization pipeline and reduce average time-to-insight for CS reps; must preserve accuracy on domain-specific terms.
- Primary persona: CS managers + triage agents.
- Data: Support transcripts (S3), small knowledge base (Confluence), and customer metadata (internal DB).

Proposed POC success criteria (please confirm):
1) Latency: median response < 350ms for 1k-token inputs in our dedicated test workload.
2) Quality: 90%+ pass rate on your 40-case evaluation set (we'll run paired A/B with your current system).
3) Cost: projected per-1k-token cost reduction >= 25% vs baseline.
4) Integration: working API flow + one-click streaming demo in your staging environment.

High-level 3-week plan
- Week 0 (this week): Kickoff, share credentials, and provide sample data + eval set.
- Week 1: Integration of SDK and API routes; basic generation and streaming tests.
- Week 2: Run evals, tune batching/quantization recommendations; set up monitoring.
- Week 3: Final validation, canary with a small user segment, handoff + next-step pricing discussion.

Owners
- ACME: Samir (technical lead), Olivia (product).
- Redwood: Marissa (commercial lead), Dev Patel (SE; implementation), Rachel Kim (CS; evaluation & monitoring).

Immediate asks
1) Please confirm success criteria above or add items by EOD Tuesday.
2) Share staging credentials for API access (read-only S3 + test DB account).
3) Book a 60-minute kickoff session — propose Wed 3/10 10am PT or Thu 3/11 9am PT.

Hi Samir / Olivia —

Quick technical follow-up ahead of kickoff with concrete integration notes so your engineers can eyeball feasibility. Summary: yes, we support SSE streaming + incremental deltas, and function/tool calling with a JSON schema contract. Below are recommended routes and snippets (also attached in sdk-integration-snippets.txt).

Auth and endpoints
- API key-based auth: provide a staging API key in header Authorization: Bearer <key>.
- Base endpoints (hosted POC): https://api.redwood.ai/v1

Primary API routes
- POST /v1/generate
  - Body: { model, input, max_tokens, top_p, temperature }
  - Use for sync generation, returns full payload when complete.
- POST /v1/stream (SSE)
  - Body: same as /generate. Server sends token-delta events (data: {"delta":"..."}) until [DONE]. Good for masking latency on long outputs.
- POST /v1/embeddings
  - For vectorizing KB & transcripts; we recommend initial embedding index of your KB and incremental upserts.

Streaming notes
- We stream token deltas as SSE with event name "token" and final event "done". Client should handle incremental partial sentences.
- We expose chunked chunk-id metadata for deterministic replay and KV-cache priming.

Function/tool-calling
- Define functions as a JSON Schema object (name, description, params schema). Example attached. Redwood will forward the parsed function call as a structured JSON in the response metadata.
- Recommended pattern: have the frontend accept the function call payload and apply a server-side validation step before any downstream writes.

Batching/quantization recommendations
- For your workload (median length ~800 tokens), enable batching with max_batch_size=8 and target latency SLO of 350ms; we'll tune dynamically.
- Quantization profile: int8-quant recommended for the cheaper profile; we'll validate quality on your eval set.

Sample curl (streaming):
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <STAGING_KEY>" -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -X POST \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-13b","input":"<prompt>","max_tokens":512}' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream

I'll bring the SDK samples and a quick demo to kickoff. If you want we can also provide a short pre-kickoff session for your engineering team (30m) to walk through auth and SSE consumption.
